title: Voice system user config
description: One file per user, read by voice-doctor.mjs, profile-build.mjs and calibrate-user.mjs. Default location: {claude}/voice/voice-config.json, or the path in VOICE_CONFIG. Every property has a default, so an empty object is a valid config. Path values may use the tokens ~ (home), {claude} (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude), {tools} (the tools dir this onboarding copy is installed in), {toolsDir} and {voiceDir} (the resolved values of paths.toolsDir and paths.voiceDir). Two rules can't be written as JSON Schema and are checked in code (lib/config.mjs): no judge in judges.allowed may come from judges.drafterLab, and judges.aiDraftsToJudges needs at least one allowed judge.

paths.description: Where the tools, the user's files and the Claude Code settings live.

toolsDir.description: The voice engine: aiscore.mjs, text-normalize.mjs, prose-gate.mjs, the detector.

voiceDir.description: The user's own voice files: samples, drafts, the calibration report. Nothing in it is shipped or uploaded.

overlay.description: The installed personal overlay, the one the scorer loads.

draftOverlay.description: Where profile-build.mjs writes a draft overlay for review. Never the installed overlay.

baseOverlay.description: An optional overlay the engine ships; when set, the personal overlay adds its checks to this one.

samplesDir.description: The user's own writing samples (.txt, .md, .mdx, .markdown, .text). Read locally, never sent anywhere.

aiDraftsDir.description: Optional AI drafts in the user's topics, for the recall check.

calibrationReport.description: Written by calibrate-user.mjs, read by voice-doctor.mjs.

settings.description: Claude Code settings file or files whose hooks section wires the voice hook.

hook.description: The voice hook script. If the settings wire a different path, the wired path is used.

sendTools.description: Tools whose calls send prose somewhere it can't be taken back. The hook BLOCKS these on a hard tell or a scorer failure. A name that starts with mcp__ is one exact tool; any other name is a tool suffix, matched under any MCP server prefix (mcp__<server>__<name>), the way the hook matches it.

nudgeGlobs.description: Files whose writes (Write, Edit, MultiEdit) get a NUDGE, never a block. The default matches the hook's prose extensions.

judges.description: The optional judge panel (prose-gate.mjs). A judge never comes from the drafter's lab: a model under-rates the tells of its own lab's writing.

mode.description: none: deterministic checks only (det-only mode; a clean draft is INCONCLUSIVE, never ADMIT). single: one judge. consensus: two judges from two other labs.

drafterLab.description: The lab whose model drafts your text (for example anthropic, google, openai, xai). Judges from this lab are not allowed.

name.description: A judge name in the gate's registry (prose-gate.mjs JUDGES).

lab.description: The lab that makes this judge's model. Must differ from drafterLab.

command.description: Optional path to the judge backend's CLI. voice-doctor checks that it is an executable file, and calibrate-user.mjs --judge-drafts passes it to the gate as OPENCODE_BIN when the environment sets none. Default: OPENCODE_BIN, then opencode on PATH.

aiDraftsToJudges.description: Allow calibrate-user.mjs --judge-drafts to send AI drafts (never your samples) to the allowed judges.

data.description: Rules for your writing samples. They are constants: the tools refuse a config that changes them.

samplesLeaveMachine.description: Samples are read locally and never sent to a model, a judge, a web tool or a remote path.

samplesToJudges.description: No judge ever sees a sample, including during calibration.

printSampleText.description: The tools print counts and sample ids, not sample text, because their output may be read into an AI session. --show-spans prints matched text for a terminal you run yourself.

level.description: standard: a held-out sample fails calibration when the gate rejects it or the send hook blocks it. strict: a nudge also counts.

detBar.description: prose-gate --det-bar: the AI-evidence score at which the deterministic layer rejects.

judgeBar.description: prose-gate --bar: the mean judge AI-ness at which the panel rejects.

heldOutShare.description: Share of samples kept out of profile building and used only to test.

minSamples.description: Below this many samples the tools still run but warn that the held-out set is small.
